purpose: Compare career and HR balance in the published e8 and new e9 game rules. Scenario simulations, not real player behavior estimates.

method.policyInputs: Current visible stats, rank, salary, job/assignment, event title/body, choice text and availability only. No check/chance, result, delta, flag or RNG input; applyChoice runs once after choice commitment. No injected state and no requestExit before a terminal screen.
method.seedDesign: Same engine seed per advertised role/attempt across four policies; independent seeded policy-choice RNG. e8/e9 cohorts differ by required prefix so paired initial RNG states are not identical.
method.promotion: Apply at every offered review whenever any application is currently available. Work prefers merit, politics prefers flattery; balanced compares visible skill/trust against lick/boss. If both unavailable train, or defer while exhausted.

policies.random: Uniform among available ordinary options, deliberate modal handling; first day never quits. Boss crisis random among signature/refusal/PIP; PIP review random merit/politics. Usually negotiates pay, then accepts.
policies.work: Text favors evidence, actual delivery, documentation and colleagues. Negotiates pay; may leave after failed negotiation when mood<25 after day9. Seeks PIP and argues by work.
policies.politics: Text favors vision/praise/obeying and avoiding confrontation. Accepts pay cut if skill<60, otherwise negotiates. Usually seeks PIP, argues by flattery.
policies.balanced: Text balances delivery, colleagues, rest and diplomacy. Extra diplomacy when boss<28; extra rest when energy/mood<28. Seeks PIP and argues with stronger visible ability.

method.selfCare: Manual self-care once available day if cash>16 and mood low (balanced42, random30, others32) or energy<22. Rest menu selected from publicly recognizable costs/preferences. Mood crisis takes paid rest if affordable, otherwise power-saving. Kind accepted only if mood<30, cash>48 and policy permits. No future result inspected.
method.completion: All policies continue until an engine terminal event, exhaustion/exit, or final career menu. No deliberate early career collection exit/demotion. Runs capped at155 choices. Executive starts manager rank2, so peak manager rate includes entry; promotedInto separates promotions from initial rank.
method.uncertainty: 95% Wilson intervals for game/attempt proportions; normal mean CI for day averages. Strategy mixtures are modeling scenarios, not estimates of actual human population probabilities. Conditional PIP/pay negotiation denominators are explicit; repeat reviews within a run are correlated, so attempt-level intervals are descriptive only.
method.replay: Every hundredth run per cell full JSON action replay equals actual final state; every final state validRun checked.

sharedSeedCaveat: The four policies share initial engine seeds within a role. Mixed-policy intervals are descriptive; individual role-policy and single-policy intervals are more interpretable. Different cohort prefixes produce independent engine sequences.

expertAssumptions.source: Extends existing public-only simulation. This script never reads choice delta, check/chance, effect, flags, result text or run RNG before committing. getEvent full object is sanitized by existing publicEvent before the policy receives it. Outcomes are observed only after selection.
expertAssumptions.merit: Targets visible skill82, trust62, boss62+. Once boss<62, unambiguous politics keyword choices get priority instead of waiting until boss28. Skill above82 has sharply diminished text weight. When boss62..78, diplomacy still receives moderate weight. Prefers merit review when available.
expertAssumptions.politics: Targets visible lick88 and boss85. Until either target is met, politics keyword choices get priority. After those targets, favors rest/cooperation; basic skill65 and trust40 retain some weight. Prefers politics review when available.
expertAssumptions.limits: Keyword recognition can misclassify natural language and neither strategy is globally optimal. Numerical targets are an experienced-player planning assumption based on visible stat meters, not a claim about real players. Both always request PIP to continue, negotiate before accepting pay cuts, never voluntarily leave after a pay negotiation, choose PIP defense from visible stronger ability (merit whenever boss<25), and choose post-PIP recovery with politics when boss<45. Both deliberately seek PIP to continue, so PIP entry is conditional strategy behavior, not an independent random-employment probability.
expertAssumptions.common: Uses baseline self-care handling plus the survival-oriented modal changes stated above and avoids intentional early exits. Engine seeds match across the two expert policies within each cohort; policy tie-break RNG is independent. Cohort prefix changes initial RNG, so e8/e9 are distribution comparisons rather than exact same dice.
